prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. New narrative scene in the same Georgian-Persian miniature series.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 17: Defeat of the Pirates, Arrival in Gulansharo & Slaying of the Chashnagir.
Setting: Gulansharo, Fatman’s flower-filled merchant courtyard near the harbor.
Scene: Disguised as a prosperous merchant, Avtandil is welcomed by Fatman beside a pool and pomegranate tree, with richly patterned textiles and the harbor’s domes glimpsed through an arch. Their guarded, attentive expressions establish the intrigue surrounding Nestan’s hidden story.
Characters: Avtandil, the YOUNG CLEAN-SHAVEN chestnut-haired man in reference2, same brown eyes/strong brows/face, but in MERCHANT DISGUISE: blue-and-warm-ochre patterned silk merchant robe, soft modest cap or uncovered wavy hair, absolutely NO HELMET, NO ARMOR, NO MAIL, NO RED MILITARY CLOAK. Fatman Khathun from reference3: mature graceful dark-haired woman, warmly expressive face with a small cheek beauty mark, gold veil and vermilion-gold courtly dress, pearl jewelry.
Story constraints: Avtandil’s face matches his portrait, but he wears merchant robes and no military helmet or armor. Chashnagir’s later killing is not simultaneous with this welcome. No pirate battle or secondary scene, no written merchandise labels.
Reference1 is STYLE ONLY (tempera, lapis/malachite/vermilion/ochre, antique gold details, softly faded ivory vellum border); do not reuse the poet. Reference2/3 are identity references only, NOT circular portrait cutouts.
Composition: horizontal16:10 approximately1600x1000, one coherent intimate encounter. Fatman stands at right welcoming the merchant-clad Avtandil at left with a gentle open-palmed gesture beside a small ornamental garden pool. Their faces large and fully visible; pomegranate tree, patterned textile cushions and the warm merchant house arcade frame them. Through a distant arch, hints of Gulansharo's blue harbor and domes. No third person, no Chashnagir watching, no inset pirate battle, no second scene.
STRICTLY NO TEXT, LETTERS, CAPTIONS, NUMBERS, CALLIGRAPHY, BANNERS, FLAGS, SCROLLS, INSCRIPTIONS, SIGNATURES OR WATERMARKS. Decorative ornament only floral/geometric, no pseudo-script.

visual_qa.notes: Avtandil is in blue merchant robes and a soft cap, with no helmet or armor; Fatman's recognizable gold veil, pearls and beauty mark. One courtyard encounter; no Chashnagir or pirate-panel conflation.
